bullets.text: A landslide known as the Ashfell Slide struck the mining region of Dreth on March 14, 2026, affecting the Withel terraces and Cranmoor.
A warning was issued for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor in the early morning, followed within the hour by the evacuation of about 60 households.
No casualties were reported in the first four hours of the response.
Government channels reported the evacuation and damage to the lower road below Withel; the cause of the slide was not yet addressed.
A warning is issued for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor and is relayed by media, NGO and government accounts.
About 60 households are evacuated from the Withel terraces.
The Ashfell slide damages the lower road at Withel.
People are moved out of the Withel terraces and Cranmoor as the evacuation continues.
The Ashfell slide damaged the lower road below the Withel terraces.
About 60 households were evacuated from the Withel terraces and Cranmoor after the warning was issued.
A landslide warning was issued for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor in the early morning.
